entries.clue: Lower the value of day geared for recreation (7)

indicatorNotes.for recreation: Recreation is re-creation, the making of a thing over again, so the letters beside it are built anew in another order.

blocks.note: d is the standard short form of day, as in D-Day
the six letters of GEARED made over into a new order

annotation.surface: A day organised around leisure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recreation' is the trap: the surface offers an afternoon off, and the setter wants re-creation, the building of something over again. Only six of the seven letters move, the day staying put in front.
annotation.definitionFit: To degrade something is to lower its worth or standing, whether a currency, a material or a reputation.

entries.clue: Ban scruffy garb amid protest, first off (7)

indicatorNotes.scruffy: Something scruffy has been thrown on anyhow, so these letters arrive in a mess rather than their proper order.
indicatorNotes.amid: What sits amid a thing sits in the middle of it, so the jumbled letters go inside the word alongside.
indicatorNotes.first off: Taking something first off is getting rid of it before anything else, and the first thing a word has is its opening letter.

blocks.note: a protest is a demo, and the demo loses its opening letter; what is left parts after its second letter
the four letters of GARB in another order

annotation.surface: A call to ban shabby clothing at demonstrations, and to do it before anything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First off' reads as the surface's 'before anything else' and works as the instruction to take a word's opening letter away. The protest is a demo, which is the word being docked.
annotation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban — on trade with a country, or on publishing a story before a set hour.

entries.clue: Assessed artist, one with a noted quiff (5)

blocks.note: an RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standing artist
a Ted is a Teddy boy, the 1950s British youth whose hair was swept up into a quiff

annotation.surface: A judgement passed on a painter with a famous hairstyle.
annotation.walkthrough: Teddy boys took their name from the Edwardian jackets they wore and their look from the greased quiff, and Ted is the short form. Nothing joins the two halves but a comma.
annotation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess it, putting a value or a rank on it, and both words are here in the past tense.

entries.clue: Turn away learner beset by shortcoming (7)

indicatorNotes.beset by: To be beset by something is to have it all round you, so the letter named is written inside the word that follows.

blocks.note: a shortcoming is a defect, and the word parts after its third letter
L is the plate a British learner driver hangs on the car

annotation.surface: A trainee hemmed in by a failing of his own.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beset by' points the opposite way to the usual: it is the learner who is beset, so the shortcoming is the thing doing the surrounding. The L comes off the plate a British learner driver carries.
annotation.definitionFit: To deflect something is to turn it away from the course it was on — a blow, a ball, or an awkward question.

entries.clue: Greek character taking in a fast dance (7)

indicatorNotes.taking in: To take something in is to admit it inside, so the word before opens up and the letter goes within.

blocks.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, and it parts after its fourth letter
the article, taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Somebody from Greece watching a quick dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' is a person in the sentence and a letter of the alphabet in the wordplay. The lambada is the Brazilian dance that swept European clubs at the end of the 1980s.
annotation.definitionFit: The lambada is a quick, close-held Brazilian dance, so 'fast dance' names its whole character.

entries.clue: Off course when on carrier? (6)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down entry what is on something else is written above it, so the first piece sits over the second.

blocks.note: as and when are the same word in 'as I arrived'
a tray is what a waiter carries the drinks on

annotation.surface: A plane losing its way after leaving the aircraft carrier.
annotation.walkthrough: The carrier the sentence pictures is the aircraft kind; the wordplay wants the thing a waiter holds. In a down clue 'on' stacks the pieces, so they land in the order you read them.
annotation.definitionFit: To go astray is to wander off the route you were meant to be on, said of a parcel, a walker or a moral.

entries.clue: Remaining cheerful with relation in the lead (7,2)

blocks.note: a thing's bearing on a matter is its relation to it, as in 'that has no bearing on the case'
a side that is up in a match is the one in the lead, two up with three to play

annotation.surface: Staying upbeat with a relative out in front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relation' is the abstract sort — how one thing bears on another — rather than the member of the family the sentence pictures. 'Up' is the scoreboard's word for being ahead.
annotation.definitionFit: Somebody bearing up is carrying trouble without letting it show, which is what remaining cheerful under it amounts to.

entries.clue: Reportedly, prepare an early version of drink (7)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: What is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word counts and its spelling does not.

blocks.note: to draft a letter or a bill is to prepare its early version, and British English says the two spellings exactly alike

annotation.surface: An instruction to knock up a first version of a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: British English keeps both spellings and gives them different jobs — one for the first version of a document, one for beer pulled from the cask — while the mouth makes no distinction at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A draught is a drink taken in one long swallow, and draught beer is the stuff drawn straight from the barrel.

entries.clue: Dismissed team getting luck? There’s slight likelihood (7,6)

blocks.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a side is a team, the word every British match report uses
what happens by chance happens by luck

annotation.surface: A knocked-out team handed a bit of luck after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dismissed' is the cricket sense, a batsman given out, and 'side' is the same game's word for a team, so the sentence keeps one sport in view while the letters assemble.
annotation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a possibility remote enough that a bookmaker would price it long, which is a slight likelihood exactly.

entries.clue: Support a thing done by punters? (4)

blocks.note: the article, taken as it stands
punters are the people putting money on the horses, and the stake they place is the bet

annotation.surface: Backing the sort of thing gamblers go in for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punter' is British for someone having a flutter on the horses, and by extension any paying customer at all. The question mark admits that a wager is only one of the things they do.
annotation.definitionFit: To abet is to back somebody up in what they are doing, the support half of 'aid and abet'.

entries.clue: French adult is excited about a cold dessert (5,5)

indicatorNotes.excited about: To be excited about a thing is to be stirred up around it, and stirred letters come out in some other order.

blocks.note: fr is the dictionary's short form of French
the seven letters of ADULT IS and the A they are excited about, eight in all, set down afresh

annotation.surface: A grown-up from France getting worked up about something chilly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adult' is usually a single letter off a film certificate, and here the whole word is fodder instead. 'Cold' belongs to the definition, not to the shuffle beside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A fruit salad is chopped fruit served in its own juice, eaten cold at the end of a meal.

entries.clue: After missing start, shorten card game (6)

indicatorNotes.After missing start: A word missing its start goes without the letter it begins with, and 'after' says the loss happens before anything else is read.

blocks.note: to abridge a book is to shorten it
the letter standing at the head of that word, and the one that goes

annotation.surface: Cutting a card game short because the beginning was missed.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb meaning to shorten is itself shortened, which is where the joke sits. Bridge is the four-handed trick-taking game played in pairs, with the bidding first and thirteen tricks after.
annotation.definitionFit: Bridge is the card game of two partnerships, descended from whist and played in clubs everywhere.

entries.clue: Possessing on board ship thin slices of wood? (8)

indicatorNotes.on board: To be on board is to be aboard, inside the vessel, so the word named is written within the ship's letters.

blocks.note: SS is the prefix on a steamship's name, and the pair parts to take what comes aboard
possessing something is having it

annotation.surface: Carrying thin slices of wood with you on a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: A plane or a chisel throws off exactly what the definition wants, and the question mark covers the fact that they need not be wood at all. 'On board ship' is the standing way of asking for something between two Ss.
annotation.definitionFit: Shavings are the thin curls a plane or a chisel peels off a piece of timber.

entries.clue: Fitter duo after surgery showing bravery (9)

indicatorNotes.after surgery: Surgery opens a thing up and closes it differently, so what went in comes out rearranged.

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder, filling the whole answer

annotation.surface: A pair of patients in better shape once the operation is over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' reads as the comparative the sentence wants, two people healthier than before, and is only letters. The bravery meant is the sort that endures pain rather than the sort that charges at things.
annotation.definitionFit: Fortitude is courage held steady under pain or hardship, the enduring kind of bravery rather than the dashing kind.

entries.clue: Tiny male priest with US college gets closing date (4,5)

blocks.note: Tim is the man's name, and Dickens's Tiny Tim is the small boy on the crutch
Eli is the priest who brings up Samuel in the Old Testament
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

annotation.surface: A small clergyman teaming up with an American university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tiny male' wants a man's name rather than a small word, and Dickens supplies it. Eli, who raises Samuel in the temple, is the crossword's standing priest, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology its standing American college.
annotation.definitionFit: A time limit is the point by which something has to be finished, which is what a closing date sets for an application.

entries.clue: Period around centre of Bath to get gemstone (5)

indicatorNotes.around: What goes around a thing is wrapped about it, so the word before splits and the next letters sit in the gap.
indicatorNotes.centre of: The centre of a word is the letters at its middle, standing the same distance from either end.

blocks.note: a period of history is an age, and the word parts after its second letter
the middle two letters of BATH, with one letter standing either side of them

annotation.surface: An era wrapped around the middle of the city of Bath.
annotation.walkthrough: Bath is a word to be measured here rather than a spa town to visit, and its middle pair is what goes inside. The stone wanted is the banded kind, sliced across to show its rings.
annotation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded, semi-precious quartz, cut and polished for brooches and marbles, which puts it among the gemstones.

entries.clue: Feature of cricket accepted by most umpires (5)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: What is accepted by something has been taken inside it, so the answer is sitting in the letters that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run straight on across the space between the two words

annotation.surface: Something in cricket that most of its officials are happy to allow.
annotation.walkthrough: The hiding place straddles the gap between two words, which is where these are hardest to spot. A stump is one of the three wooden posts the bowler aims at, and three of them make a wicket.
annotation.definitionFit: The stumps are the wooden posts that stand up as a cricket wicket, so one of them is a feature of the game.

entries.clue: Voracious insect? Call it close to bothersome (7)

indicatorNotes.close to: The close of a word is where it finishes, so only its last letter is taken.

blocks.note: to term a thing something is to call it that
the word taken as it stands
the letter BOTHERSOME finishes on

annotation.surface: Calling a greedy insect something not far short of annoying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to bothersome' reads as an estimate, nearly annoying, and is really the instruction to take one letter. Termites eat the timber of a house from the inside, which is where the voracious comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Termites chew through wood day and night in colonies of millions, which makes the insect a byword for voracious.

entries.clue: Go along with account by set of actors (9)

blocks.note: ac is the short form of account on a bank statement
a theatre company is the set of actors who perform together

annotation.surface: Agreeing with the version of events a troupe of actors gives.
annotation.walkthrough: A company is the standing troupe attached to a playhouse, which is the set of actors meant. The definition covers both walking beside somebody and playing the piano behind a singer.
annotation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to go along with them, on a journey or at the keyboard behind their singing.

entries.clue: Left out diet Tom cooked (7)

indicatorNotes.cooked: Cooking turns what goes into the pot into something else, so the letters come out in a different arrangement.

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder, filling the whole answer

annotation.surface: Tom's home-cooked diet meal, abandoned on the side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as food going cold on the worktop and means excluded. Tom is here for his three letters, which is what first names are usually for.
annotation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out — a name off a list, a verse skipped in a hymn.

entries.clue: Part of a hooter? (7)

blocks.note: the phrase asks for a component of whatever is named next, not a synonym for it
the surface hears a car horn or an owl; British slang calls a large nose a hooter, and that is the sense meant

annotation.surface: One piece of something that hoots.
annotation.walkthrough: Hooter is British for a nose, usually a sizeable one, and the same word does duty for a car horn and an owl. The question mark is the only warning that a joke is being made.
annotation.definitionFit: A hooter is the British nickname for a nose, and a nose is built round a pair of nostrils.

entries.clue: Remaining lot of students in university education (6)

indicatorNotes.in: What is in a thing sits inside it, so the students are written between the two halves that follow.

blocks.note: u is the short form of university
the NUS is the National Union of Students, the body British undergraduates belong to
ed is the short form of education

annotation.surface: The students still left on a university course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lot' is a crowd rather than a quantity, and this crowd has a name: the National Union of Students. The two words that follow give up a letter each and part to let them in.
annotation.definitionFit: What is unused has not been touched, so it is what remains once everything else has gone.

entries.clue: Rail sank badly in island nation (3,5)

indicatorNotes.badly: Something done badly has not come out as it should, so the letters are set down out of their proper order.

blocks.note: eight letters of fodder, filling both words of the answer

annotation.surface: A length of railing going down badly somewhere overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is a marsh bird as well as a metal bar, which is what lets the sentence almost mean something. The country was called Ceylon until 1972.
annotation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is the island republic off the southern tip of India, a country with no land border at all.

entries.clue: Where one might put holiday clothes if needed? (2,4)

annotation.definition: Where one might put holiday clothes
annotation.definitionNote: The first definition answers a question of place instead of naming a thing, and it wants an article the answer does not print — in a case — which the question mark covers.

blocks.clueFragment: Where one might put holiday clothes
blocks.note: the suitcase open on the bed, which is where the packing goes
the phrase for taking a thing along against a need that may never arise

annotation.surface: Packing for a trip and wondering where everything should go.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves belong to the same holiday: the bag things are packed into, and the reason the spare jumper goes in at all. The first reading quietly drops an article.
annotation.definitionFit: Packed clothes go in a case; and to take an umbrella in case is to take it should it be needed.

entries.clue: Top sportsperson found in Altrincham, possibly (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: What is found in something was already sitting there, so the answer is read straight out of the letters that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run on across the comma and into the word after it

annotation.surface: A star athlete who might well come from Altrincham.
annotation.walkthrough: Altrincham is a town in Greater Manchester, and 'possibly' looks like the usual hedge on a definition by example while really supplying the last letter. Champ is the short, breezy form of champion.
annotation.definitionFit: The champ is the champion, the boxer or the runner who has beaten everybody else in the division.

entries.clue: Ace site Sam devised for whiskery pet (7,3)

indicatorNotes.devised: What is devised has been put together from scratch, so these letters are arranged into something they were not before.

blocks.note: ten letters of fodder, filling both words of the answer

annotation.surface: Sam putting together a first-rate website.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ace' is the sentence's compliment to the website and is nothing but fodder. The breed meant is the cream-coated cat with the dark face and the famously loud voice, out of what is now Thailand.
annotation.definitionFit: A Siamese is a slender, blue-eyed breed kept as a house cat, and like every cat it comes with a full set of whiskers.

entries.clue: Those succeeding on radio producing tunes (4)

indicatorNotes.on radio: What comes over the radio is heard and never seen, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling.

blocks.note: those who succeed to a title or an estate are its heirs, and the aitch in that word is silent

annotation.surface: Broadcasters who are doing well and putting out music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' is the inheritance sense rather than the doing-well one. An air is an old word for a melody, kept alive in titles like 'Londonderry Air'.
annotation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, the sense that survives mostly in the names of old songs.

entries.clue: Examine again note by boss before end of holiday (7)

indicatorNotes.end of: The end of a word is the letter it stops at, and that letter alone is taken.

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, doh re mi
a boss is the raised knob on a shield or a door, which is a stud
the letter HOLIDAY finishes on

annotation.surface: Going over your notes with the manager before the holiday runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the metalwork sense, the raised stud on a shield or a church door, not the person in charge the sentence hires. Re is the sol-fa note, the one between doh and mi.
annotation.definitionFit: The re- prefix means over again, so restudying a subject is giving it a second examination rather than a first.

entries.clue: A department largely emptied in a skilful manner (7)

indicatorNotes.emptied: A thing emptied keeps its walls and loses everything between them, so only the outside letters of the word stay.

blocks.note: the article, taken as it stands
dept is the standard short form of department on an office directory
the first and last letters of LARGELY, everything between them gone

annotation.surface: A government department mostly cleared out, and neatly done too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like the adverb doing the measuring — mostly emptied — and is the word being emptied itself. The department shortens the way it does on an office door.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone adept is skilled at what they do, and the adverb says the thing was carried out in that skilful way.
